US officials stated that Patriot and THAAD interceptors in Europe have reached levels described as 'beyond critical.' These shortages complicate US contingency plans for defending Taiwan and limit support for Ukraine. Rebuilding stocks from allies like Japan and Germany could take years, leaving significant gaps in military readiness.
items.title: Iran conflict strains US missile stocks and complicates defense against China and Russia

key_points: India and Uzbekistan have agreed to upgrade their bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership.
Both countries set a target of USD 5 billion in annual trade by 2030.
The two nations will establish a framework for long-term uranium supply from Uzbekistan to India.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred Uzbekistan's prestigious 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev agreed to elevate bilateral relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The leaders announced a target of USD 5 billion in annual trade by 2030, up from the current volume of over USD 1 billion. Both nations will establish a framework for long-term uranium supply and encourage co-development of military hardware. Modi was conferred Uzbekistan's prestigious 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order, which he dedicated to the enduring bond between the two countries. The agreement also includes plans to restore ancient Buddhist sites and elevate joint commissions to a ministerial level.
items.title: India-Uzbekistan upgrade ties to strategic partnership; Modi receives highest Uzbek honour

key_points: India supplied nearly one million barrels of gasoline to Russia over the past two months.
Russian seaborne gasoline imports reached a record 125,000 barrels per day in August.
Approximately 55% of Russia's August gasoline imports arrived on sanctioned tonnage.
India imported more than 2.6 million barrels per day of Russian crude in June and July.
items.summary: Ship-tracking data cited by PTI shows India supplied nearly one million barrels of gasoline to Russia in two months. Vortexa reports Russian gasoline imports hit a record 125,000 barrels per day in August due to Ukrainian attacks on refineries. The article notes that around 55% of these imports arrived on sanctioned tonnage via dark ship-to-ship transfers. India's role as a supplier grows alongside its increased purchases of Russian crude oil.
items.title: India supplies record gasoline to Russia as Ukrainian attacks disrupt local refining

key_points: A 31-member Kerala group returned safely to Kochi after being stranded by flash floods in Nepal.
Group members stated that a 20-minute delay at a Buddha temple prevented them from crossing a bridge that was subsequently washed away.
They described seeing buildings swept away within seconds and spending a difficult night without food.
Emotional reunions occurred at the airport as families reunited with the travellers.
items.summary: A 31-member Kerala group returned safely to Kochi after being stranded by flash floods in Nepal. Group members stated that a 20-minute delay at a Buddha temple prevented them from crossing a bridge that was subsequently washed away. They described seeing buildings swept away within seconds and spending a difficult night without food. Emotional reunions occurred at the airport as families reunited with the travellers.
items.title: Kerala group credits 20-minute temple delay for survival in Nepal floods

key_points: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will inaugurate the first phase of the Veligonda irrigation project on August 31, 2026.
The government plans to release 10.70 TMC of Krishna water into the Nallamala Sagar reservoir during the inauguration.
The initial phase aims to provide irrigation to 1.19 lakh acres and drinking water to approximately four lakh people.
Accelerated construction following the 2024 NDA government's assumption of office helped overcome previous delays in the project.
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will inaugurate the first phase of the Veligonda irrigation project on August 31, 2026. The government plans to release 10.70 TMC of Krishna water into the Nallamala Sagar reservoir. This initiative aims to provide irrigation to 1.19 lakh acres and drinking water to approximately four lakh people in the initial phase. The project addresses decades of water scarcity and aims to reduce groundwater dependence. Accelerated construction following the 2024 NDA government's assumption of office helped overcome previous delays.
items.title: AP Chief Minister Naidu to inaugurate Veligonda irrigation project phase one

key_points: HDFC Bank is likely to appoint Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha or an external candidate as its next CEO.
Two people familiar with the matter stated the bank is searching for an external candidate to meet RBI requirements.
The CEO search follows six months of leadership upheaval and a 27% drop in HDFC Bank shares this year.
Kaizad Bharucha is eligible for the position as he will have served as a full-time director for 15 years by 2029.
items.summary: HDFC Bank is evaluating Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and an external candidate for its next CEO following Sashidhar Jagdishan's retirement. Two unnamed sources confirmed the bank is seeking multiple names to comply with Reserve Bank of India regulations. The leadership search follows recent governance controversies and a 27% share price decline this year. Bharucha, who oversees retail and wholesale businesses, is eligible for the role after his 15-year directorship term.
items.title: HDFC Bank considers internal and external candidates for new CEO

key_points: Regen Fiber opened a Fairfax, Iowa, facility in 2024 to mechanically recycle retired wind turbine blades.
The company avoids heat and chemicals to convert blades into fibers and powders for concrete and asphalt.
Jeff Woods of parent company Travero stated the process recycles 100 percent of each blade.
The site is expected to process over 30,000 tons annually on a one-shift schedule.
items.summary: Regen Fiber opened a Fairfax, Iowa, facility in 2024 to mechanically recycle retired wind turbine blades. The company avoids heat and chemicals to convert blades into fibers and powders for concrete and asphalt. Jeff Woods of parent company Travero stated the process recycles 100 percent of each blade. The site is expected to process over 30,000 tons annually on a one-shift schedule. Regen Fiber also operates facilities in Des Moines and Lubbock for different blade materials.
items.title: Regen Fiber recycles Iowa wind turbine blades into road materials

He noted that 3.5 million women have received benefits since the 2020 launch, with 350,000 currently expanding their businesses.
The government has disbursed ₹19,203 crore to 7.8 million beneficiaries according to the scheme's portal.
Modi also urged content creators to produce material in various languages to combat drug addiction among youth.

items.title: PM Modi says women make up 46% of PM SVANidhi beneficiaries

key_points: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan decided not to seek another term as Managing Director and CEO.
The board has accelerated the process of identifying a successor due to the shortened timeline.
Analysts predict potential share price volatility driven by headline risks and management stability concerns.
Investors are likely to focus on corporate governance and leadership succession planning in the coming months.
items.summary: HDFC Bank announced that CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan will not seek reappointment, prompting the board to accelerate finding a successor. The bank noted Jagdishan's three-decade tenure and his role in a major merger. Analysts suggest share prices may face volatility due to leadership changes and recent governance concerns. Investors are expected to monitor the transition closely for future growth signals.
items.title: HDFC Bank CEO steps down as board accelerates successor search

key_points: The Madhya Pradesh BJP launched a two-day state executive meeting in Orchha on Sunday.
Sources indicated that the 2028 Assembly election strategy and expanding Gen Z outreach are the key agenda items.
The party plans to formulate a strategy to engage young people and address their specific issues.
Senior leaders attributed the recent Datia Assembly bypoll loss partly to youth dissatisfaction.
The executive committee will review organizational measures and decide the party's future course of action.
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh BJP began a two-day executive meeting in Orchha on Sunday, with sources stating that strategies for the 2028 Assembly elections and outreach to the Gen Z generation are the primary focus. The ruling party plans to establish dialogue with young people to understand their priorities and address their concerns. Approximately 300 delegates, including Chief Minister Mohan Yadav and Union ministers, are attending the event. Party leaders noted that youth dissatisfaction was a factor in the recent Datia Assembly bypoll defeat. The meeting will also review organizational strength at the booth level and discuss themes like 'Samarasta Ka Sankalp' and 'Viksit Bharat 2047'.
items.title: MP BJP starts two-day Orchha meet focusing on Gen Z outreach and 2028 polls

key_points: A 50-year-old man died after his neck became trapped in a hospital lift in Rewa.
His son reported the patient was being moved to an upper floor when the lift malfunctioned.
Family members allege hospital staff prevented them from helping and ignored a prior entrapment.
Police are investigating the incident while the family protests outside the hospital.
items.summary: A 50-year-old patient died after becoming trapped in a lift at a private hospital in Rewa on Saturday. His son stated the man had recently suffered a broken shoulder and was being moved to an upper floor when the incident occurred. Family members allege that hospital staff prevented them from entering the lift and failed to ensure safety after another person was trapped earlier. Relatives staged a protest demanding the hospital shut down while police collect evidence regarding the breakdown and the death.
items.title: 50-Year-Old Man Dies After Getting Trapped In Lift At Rewa Hospital

key_points: Sonam Wangchuk assessed CJP founders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka as having political ambitions during the Jantar Mantar protest.
Wangchuk told Prakhar Gupta that having political ambitions is normal and not wrong for young leaders.
The activist advised the founders to keep the student movement platform neutral and free from any specific party agenda.
Wangchuk expressed happiness that the founders maintained the platform's apolitical nature throughout the nearly two-month protest.
items.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk stated that Cockroach Janta Party founders possess political ambitions, a conclusion he reached during the Jantar Mantar protest. Wangchuk told Prakhar Gupta that while the founders are not saints, having such ambitions is not wrong. He encouraged young leaders to join politics but urged them to keep the student movement platform neutral and apolitical. Wangchuk noted he had previously warned the founders to maintain the platform's sanctity while pursuing their goals.
items.title: Sonam Wangchuk says CJP founders have political ambitions

key_points: Delhi Police arrested a 35-year-old attendant after a three-year-old boy was allegedly tied to a chair and assaulted at a Maujpur playschool.
The child's parents noticed physical injuries and behavioral changes, leading them to request CCTV footage which staff initially obstructed.
Video recordings captured the toddler being pulled by his ears, tied to a chair, kicked, and repeatedly struck.
Police registered a case under the POCSO Act and BNS while investigating the roles of the school's director and principal.
items.summary: Delhi Police arrested a 35-year-old attendant following allegations of severe abuse against a three-year-old boy at a Maujpur playschool. The child's parents discovered injuries and behavioral changes, prompting a request for CCTV footage that staff initially obstructed. Video recordings showed the toddler being tied to a chair, kicked, and struck. Police registered a case under the POCSO Act and BNS, while investigating the roles of the director and principal.
items.title: Delhi police arrest attendant after toddler tied to chair and assaulted at playschool

key_points: Bihar Congress leaders formally notified Mallikarjun Kharge of an intended peaceful sit-in outside party headquarters in New Delhi on 8 September.
The protest is contingent on the removal of national in-charge Krishna Allavaru and State president Rajesh Kumar.
Delegation members allege disorder and arbitrary ticket distribution within the Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee following the 2025 Assembly election.
Senior leader Kishore Kumar Jha suggested the workers' grievances could be addressed through dialogue rather than confrontation.
items.summary: Bihar Congress leaders have notified party president Mallikarjun Kharge of a planned sit-in protest in New Delhi on 8 September. The demonstration seeks the removal of national in-charge Krishna Allavaru and State president Rajesh Kumar following the party's poor 2025 election performance. Delegation members allege disorder and arbitrary ticket distribution within the Bihar unit. Senior leader Kishore Kumar Jha suggested grievances could be addressed through dialogue rather than confrontation.
items.title: Bihar Congress Leaders Plan Delhi Protest Over Leadership Changes

key_points: The Quint verified that a graphic video circulating on social media is not from India.
The footage depicts a rape and murder case involving 28-year-old Shampa Khatun in Bangladesh's Madaripur.
Faruk Mollah was arrested in connection with the assault and killing of the woman.
The video is being falsely shared to allege that BJP workers killed a child in West Bengal.
items.summary: The Quint fact-checked a viral video claiming to show a child murdered by BJP workers in West Bengal. The outlet confirmed the footage is false, originating instead from a rape and murder case in Bangladesh's Madaripur district. Reports identified the victim as 28-year-old Shampa Khatun, whose body was found in Shibchar. Faruk Mollah was arrested in connection with the crime. The Quint stated the video is being misused to spread misinformation about the alleged attack in India.
items.title: Video of Bangladesh rape-murder falsely shared as West Bengal BJP attack

key_points: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences rescheduled the NEET-PG 2026 exam for nearly 300 candidates at the Sitapura centre to September 5.
ADM Narendra Verma stated that technical failures prevented the exam from proceeding properly at the venue.
Candidate Vishnu Sharma protested the repeated system crashes and demanded a nationwide cancellation and re-conducting of the exam.
The board will share further venue details and issue revised admit cards separately.
items.summary: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences rescheduled the NEET-PG 2026 exam for nearly 300 candidates at the Sitapura centre to September 5 due to a power outage. ADM Narendra Verma stated that technical failures prevented the exam from proceeding properly. Candidate Vishnu Sharma protested the repeated system crashes and demanded a nationwide cancellation and re-conducting of the exam. The board will share further venue details and issue revised admit cards separately.
items.title: NEET-PG exam rescheduled for 300 candidates after Sitapura power outage

Morgan Terrassen sold its entire stake in the company for ₹678.6 crore, marking a complete exit.

The chemical stock has gained 27% in a month despite weak market sentiments.
items.summary: Narayan Murthy's family office Catamaran Ventures purchased 55,978 shares of Foseco India on Thursday, while Morgan Stanley and LIC Mutual Fund also participated in block deals. Morgan Terrassen sold its entire stake in the company for ₹678.6 crore. Foseco India reported a 14.42% rise in revenue to ₹48 crore in Q1 FY27, with net profit increasing 78.31% to ₹10 crore. The chemical stock has gained 27% in a month despite weak market sentiments.
items.title: Narayan Murthy family and Morgan Stanley buy Foseco India shares

Three first information reports were registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to unlawful assembly and assault.
Police allege that unknown persons obstructed officials and assaulted personnel while removing the signboard.
The TMC alleges that municipal officials trespassed and assaulted party staff without providing a valid notice.

Police allege that unknown persons obstructed officials and assaulted personnel while removing the board. Conversely, the TMC claims municipal officials trespassed and assaulted party staff without a valid notice.
items.title: Kolkata Police summon TMC leaders over signboard removal clash

key_points: Kanupriya Dhingra distinguishes between the Delhi Amrita Pritam lived in and the Delhi she wrote about in her fiction and poetry.
Pritam resided in Delhi for 58 years, working at All India Radio and editing the magazine Nagmani from her Hauz Kaus home.
Her literary works often portrayed the city as a place of decay, isolation, and gendered oppression rather than a sanctuary.
The convergence of her lived and written experiences occurred when her house was demolished five years after her death.
Dhingra argues that while Pritam's physical address was erased, her literary legacy survives through translations and secondhand copies.
items.summary: Kanupriya Dhingra explores the distinct relationship between writer Amrita Pritam and Delhi, distinguishing the city she inhabited from the one she depicted in her work. Pritam lived in Delhi from 1947 until her death in 2005, working at All India Radio and editing the literary magazine Nagmani from her Hauz Khas home. While the city eventually honored her with an honorary doctorate and Rajya Sabha nomination, her writings frequently indicted Delhi as a place of sickened values and isolation. The two versions of the city converged only when her son sold and demolished her house five years after her death. Dhingra notes that Pritam's poem 'Mera Pata' renounces a fixed address, a stance the city eventually mirrored by erasing her physical home.
items.title: Amrita Pritam lived in Delhi but wrote about a different city

key_points: Seven of India's top 10 firms lost a combined Rs 1.13 lakh crore in market capitalization last week.
Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking Ltd cited global interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty as causes for the market correction.
Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries recorded the largest market cap declines, while TCS, ICICI Bank, and SBI gained value.
The BSE Sensex fell 276.32 points and the NSE Nifty dropped 76.35 points during the week.
items.summary: Seven of India's top 10 companies saw their market capitalization drop by Rs 1.13 lakh crore last week. Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking Ltd attributed the decline to global interest rate concerns and geopolitical uncertainty. Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries faced the steepest valuation losses, while TCS, ICICI Bank, and SBI were the only winners among the top ten. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty indices also dipped during the period.
items.title: Seven top Indian firms lost Rs 1.13 lakh crore in market cap last week

key_points: Nepal officials requested India to advance power import approvals to September due to flood-induced generation deficits.
The flash flood reduced Nepal's electricity generation capacity by about 550 megawatts.
India imported 3,299 million units of power from Nepal during fiscal year 2025-26.
An Indian official stated the national grid can absorb a 400 megawatt shortfall without disruption.
Authorities reported the flood killed approximately 675 people in Nepal-Tibet border regions.
items.summary: Senior officials in Nepal's Union Power Ministry stated that Kathmandu has asked India to advance electricity import approvals starting in September due to generation deficits. The flash flood damaged infrastructure, reducing Nepal's generation capacity by approximately 550 megawatts. Officials noted that India imported 3,299 million units from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26. An Indian official confirmed the country can absorb the 400 megawatt shortfall without disrupting grid stability. The disaster killed about 675 people in Nepal-Tibet border regions.
items.title: Nepal requests early power imports from India following flood damage

key_points: The Union Petroleum Ministry stated that the revised CBG offtake framework will not cause a material price impact.
The ministry assured that government-funded support and a wider gas pool would sustainably cushion the pricing.
The Union Cabinet approved the GOBARdhan scheme on August 6, setting the CBG offtake price at ₹2,110 per MMBtu.
Officials explained that the government provides an affordability cushion of ₹10 per kilogram of CBG.
items.summary: The Union Petroleum Ministry stated that the revised CBG offtake framework will not cause a material price impact. The ministry assured that government-funded support and a wider gas pool would sustainably cushion the pricing. The Union Cabinet approved the GOBARdhan scheme on August 6, setting the CBG offtake price at ₹2,110 per MMBtu. Officials explained that the government provides an affordability cushion of ₹10 per kilogram of CBG. The ministry clarified that the net cost is spread across a domestic gas base 2.5 to 3 times larger than before.
items.title: Government ensures no material price impact on CBG with revised offtake framework

key_points: Gene Marks states that small businesses are learning from large corporations' AI investments to avoid costly errors.
The author reports that SMBs successfully apply AI to software development, security, and customer service without publicizing payroll reductions.
Marks writes that small companies are hesitant to trust autonomous AI agents, preferring to use the technology for analysis instead.
The article concludes that small business owners should let large corporations test ambitious AI predictions while focusing on practical applications.
items.summary: Gene Marks writes that small businesses are benefiting from large corporations' AI experiments by adopting successful tools while avoiding costly mistakes. The author notes that SMBs use AI for software development, security, and customer service without making headlines about payroll cuts. Companies are also cautious about trusting autonomous agents, preferring to analyze data rather than replace staff. Ultimately, Marks suggests letting big corporations test ambitious AI predictions while small firms focus on practical, common-sense applications.
items.title: Small businesses learn AI lessons from big corporate failures and successes

key_points: Positive AI sentiment among US workers fell from 81 percent in 2019 to 43 percent by mid-2026 according to Glassdoor.
Gen Z women represent the most skeptical workforce demographic with only 21 percent of their AI-related comments being positive.
Managers remain the most optimistic group, whereas insurance claim adjusters and customer service representatives view AI almost entirely negatively.
Fear of job loss is the single most common complaint, accounting for 20 percent of negative reviews.
items.summary: A Glassdoor analysis indicates that positive sentiment regarding AI among US workers dropped from 81 percent in 2019 to 43 percent by mid-2026. The report highlights significant demographic divides, noting that Gen Z women are the most skeptical group with only 21 percent positive comments. While executives remain optimistic, roles like insurance claim adjusters and customer service representatives view AI almost universally negatively. Fear of job loss accounts for 20 percent of negative reviews, though many workers also complain about forced adoption and unrealistic productivity expectations. The data suggests that once a role encounters moderate AI exposure, criticism appears regardless of actual automation threats.
items.title: Glassdoor analysis shows US worker sentiment toward AI has sharply declined

key_points: Aaron Regunberg reports that opposition to datacenters is uniting voters across the political spectrum against tech oligarchs.
The article states that many Democratic leaders remain aligned with big tech despite widespread local resistance to new projects.
Regunberg warns that failing to address this issue could allow far-right nationalists to exploit the backlash.
The author argues this movement offers a singular chance to redirect American polarization toward economic grievances.
items.summary: Aaron Regunberg reports that growing opposition to big tech datacenters is creating a rare opportunity to unite Americans across partisan lines. Organizers note that residents from diverse political backgrounds are increasingly viewing these projects as a shared threat to their communities. The article highlights how this movement challenges the traditional left-right divide by focusing anger on billionaire interests rather than cultural issues. However, Democrats face significant hurdles as many party leaders remain aligned with the tech industry despite local backlash. Regunberg warns that failing to capitalize on this moment could allow far-right forces to exploit the issue for nationalist agendas. The piece argues that the current political landscape offers a unique chance to redirect polarization toward structural economic problems. Ultimately, the author suggests that seizing this opportunity requires Democrats to genuinely listen to constituents opposed to datacenter construction.
items.title: Datacenter opposition may reshape US politics by uniting voters against tech oligarchs

key_points: Slate Auto confirmed a high roof cargo topper will be available to all buyers of its $25,000 compact pickup.
Christian Kreipke, the company's Fleet Business Development Lead, stated the kit costs around $3,000 and offers standard and high-roof options.
The executive noted municipalities are already planning uses like refrigeration units and mobile vending machines.
Kreipke also said the truck will keep its basic dimensions to help third-party manufacturers build equipment.
items.summary: Slate Auto confirmed a high roof cargo topper will be available to all buyers of its $25,000 compact pickup. Christian Kreipke, the company's Fleet Business Development Lead, stated the kit costs around $3,000 and offers standard and high-roof options. The executive noted municipalities are already planning uses like refrigeration units and mobile vending machines. Kreipke also said the truck will keep its basic dimensions to help third-party manufacturers build equipment.
items.title: Slate Auto confirms high roof cargo kit for its compact pickup truck

key_points: Tiger GSE launched the Tiger Li-Ion electric baggage tug with a 60,000 lb payload capacity.
Waev claims fleet operators can save more than $19,000 per year in fuel costs per tug.
The electric tug reduces carbon emissions by over 3.5 tons annually per unit.
The vehicle offers up to 60 miles of range and includes multiple safety features.
items.summary: Tiger GSE has introduced the Tiger Li-Ion electric baggage tug, designed to replace diesel-powered ground support equipment at airports. The company reports that fleet operators could save over $19,000 annually per unit in fuel costs while reducing carbon emissions by more than 3.5 tons per year. Waev president and CEO Keith Simon stated that the future of ground support equipment is electric to meet sustainability goals. The vehicle features a 48 kWh battery pack offering up to 60 miles of range and includes safety features like anti-rollover technology and an operator sensor.
items.title: Tiger GSE launches electric baggage tug with 60,000 lb capacity

key_points: A lawsuit alleges West Point fired Dr. Adam Kalkstein for refusing to stop teaching about human causes of climate change.
Kalkstein described the order to remove the curriculum content as immoral and potentially illegal.
This is the second legal action at West Point concerning academic freedom under the current administration.
West Point acknowledged the allegations but declined further comment citing pending litigation.
items.summary: A lawsuit claims West Point fired Dr. Adam Kalkstein after he refused an order to stop teaching about human causes of the climate emergency. Kalkstein, a civilian geography professor, stated that removing this content would be immoral and potentially illegal. Brig. Gen. Shane Reeves allegedly stormed out of a meeting after Kalkstein challenged the directive. This incident marks the second legal action at the academy regarding academic freedom under the current administration. Kalkstein's attorney described him as a conservative Republican loyal to the cadets who believes military students must know the truth about the climate crisis. The lawsuit alleges the academy breached Kalkstein's First Amendment rights. West Point acknowledged the allegations but declined further comment due to pending litigation. The article notes President Trump has previously labeled the climate emergency a hoax while also attempting cultural changes in military institutions.
items.title: West Point fires climate scientist who taught human causes of climate change

key_points: The author predicts US gas cars will lose transportation value by 2031 as cheap used EVs become available.
Norway and China are cited as proof that new and used car markets are shifting away from internal combustion engines.
The author calculates that a typical gas car costs about $300 a month to own compared to $300 for a used EV.
Several factors like charging access and truck availability could delay the predicted value collapse in the US.
The author warns car manufacturers that continuing to invest in gas tooling is a risky bet against the used EV market.
items.summary: The author reports a five-year prediction that ordinary gasoline and diesel cars in the US will become worth less than zero as transportation by 2031. This forecast relies on Norway and China serving as leading indicators for the global shift toward electric vehicles. Norway effectively ended new internal combustion engine sales in 2025, while China saw used gasoline car values drop significantly as electric vehicle adoption surged. The author argues that total cost of ownership for electric vehicles will soon undercut gas cars, forcing owners to sell or face high running costs. However, the author acknowledges several conditions could delay this outcome, including the lack of cheap used electric trucks and limited home charging access for many Americans. The author notes that exporting unwanted gas cars to other markets might temporarily postpone the value collapse in the US. Ultimately, the author suggests that if used electric vehicles become plentiful and affordable, the residual value of gas cars will collapse regardless of current US market conditions.
items.title: Author bets US gas cars will lose value by 2031

items.summary: An op-ed by CleanTechnica reflects on the death of King Harald V of Norway, who died on August 28, 2026, at age 89. While tax breaks explain part of Norway's success, the article highlights the royal household's visible adoption of electric vehicles as a key signal. Harald V also spent roughly 20 years as WWF Norway president, validating youth climate concerns through New Year addresses. The piece notes that Norway's 97.6% EV sales figure relies on a grid powered by roughly 98% renewable electricity. The author concludes that the King's consistent modeling of green behavior made environmental protection a national identity rather than a partisan issue.
items.title: Op-Ed: Norway's King Harald V championed clean tech through soft power

items.summary: Jewellery designer Constantina Makridakis explains how her unique condition, synaesthesia, allows her to taste names and voices. Neufeld estimates that 2 to 4 percent of the global population experiences this phenomenon, though many remain unaware of it. Makridakis describes how specific names trigger distinct flavors, such as her father's name tasting like caramel-coated chocolate. She also highlights how these perceptions can be distracting or lead to cravings, such as wanting Coca-Cola when hearing an American accent. Both Makridakis and Neufeld emphasize that synaesthesia demonstrates how individuals perceive the world differently despite sharing common sensory inputs.

The government argued that closer ties would help address economic pressures and Arctic security concerns. Opponents focused on protecting fishing rights and national sovereignty. Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir pledged to respect the outcome, making it unlikely that negotiations will resume before her term ends in 2028. Iceland will continue its current relationship with the bloc through the European Economic Area and Schengen zone.

items.summary: UNESCO added six historic plantation estates, known as 'rocas', to its World Heritage List last month, highlighting their significance in the history of forced labor. Conceicao Moreno, a National Assembly member and descendant of plantation workers, emphasized the deep cultural connection these sites hold for the community. While most estates remain in disrepair, investment firm HBD is renovating two sites into hotels to generate employment and preserve the architecture. Culture chief Emir Boa Morte stated that this recognition aims to mobilize the population and restore the buildings over the next decade. Officials insist that new development will not erase history but will instead combine the past with present uses. UNESCO noted the sites illustrate a large-scale colonial agro-industrial system based on forced migration from the late 19th to mid-20th century.
items.title: UNESCO recognition boosts preservation efforts for Sao Tome historic plantations

items.summary: India likely grew at more than 7% last quarter, yet this pace may not achieve Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a developed nation by 2047. Ashok Lahiri, a senior official at the country's apex government-run think tank, states that reaching this status requires the world's sixth-largest economy to grow at 9.25% annually for 21 years. While the Viksit Bharat initiative is a centerpiece of Modi's third term, several economists warn that assuming the current growth rate, India's economy would fall short of this ambitious target.
items.title: India's 7% growth may fall short of Modi's 2047 developed nation dream

key_points: One Nation candidate Luke Herdegen defeated the Labor Party in a Western Australia special election.
The state electoral commission reported Herdegen held 57% of the vote with 75% of ballots counted.
Broadcaster ABC called the by-election for Herdegen following the result.
Longtime Labor lawmaker Paul Papalia retired from the seat due to a family illness.
items.summary: Australia's far-right One Nation party secured its first lower house seat in Western Australia by defeating the ruling Labor Party in a special election. With 75% of votes counted, One Nation candidate Luke Herdegen held 57% of the vote, according to the state electoral commission. Broadcaster ABC called the by-election for Herdegen, marking a significant shift from last year's results where Labor won the area. The special election was triggered when longtime Labor lawmaker Paul Papalia announced his retirement due to a family illness.
items.title: One Nation party wins Western Australia special election seat

key_points: Italy plans to put all 12,000 paid beaches up for public tender by September 30, 2027.
The European Commission considers Italy in breach of the 2009 Bolkestein directive on free competition.
Legambiente reports that private concessions currently occupy more than 42% of the country's coastline.
The state collects between €80m and €100m annually from concessions while the sector earns over €2 billion.
items.summary: Italy aims to reform its beach concession system by introducing public tenders for all 12,000 paid beaches by September 30, 2027. The European Commission has pressured Rome to comply with the 2009 Bolkestein directive regarding free competition. Current private operators manage over 42% of the coastline, according to Legambiente, while the state collects between €80m and €100m annually. Critics warn that new tenders could displace traditional family-owned businesses in favor of large tourism groups.
items.title: Italy plans to reform its 12,000 private beaches by 2027

key_points: Residents of Narsarsuaq fear displacement if the United States reopens its former military base.
The US administration is negotiating to expand its military presence and demand sovereignty over new defense zones.
Local farmers oppose uranium mining and worry about US interest in Greenland's natural resources.
The European Union is pushing for increased investment and respect for Greenlandic self-determination.
Greenland authorities halted a US-linked oil exploration project due to lack of permits.
items.summary: The article reports that residents of Narsarsuaq, a remote settlement in southern Greenland, are increasingly concerned about the potential return of United States military presence and the exploitation of local natural resources. Ole Guldager, a local historian, stated that the community fears losing their homes if American troops reoccupy the former base. The United States has been negotiating with Danish and Greenlandic representatives to expand its military footprint, demanding sovereignty over the territory of future installations. Meanwhile, Aviaja Lennert, a farmer near the Kvanefjeld rare earth deposit, expressed worry about uranium extraction and US interest in the island's wealth. The European Union is attempting to strengthen its influence by proposing increased investment and urging respect for Greenlandic sovereignty. Barry Andrews, an Irish MEP, emphasized that Greenland's sovereignty must be respected and that the EU should be the island's preferred partner. Despite these diplomatic efforts, the Greenland government recently ordered a postponement of a controversial oil exploration project linked to US interests.
items.title: Residents fear US military return and mining threats in southern Greenland

key_points: Arthur Kermalvezen and Audrey, both donor-conceived in Paris, feared they were half-siblings before dating.
French laws restrict genetic testing, forcing the couple to rely on an illegal doctor or a home kit ordered abroad.
Audrey discovered her biological sister was a client she had represented in court after DNA testing.
Their campaign contributed to legal changes allowing future donor-conceived individuals to access donor information.
items.summary: Arthur Kermalvezen and Audrey, both donor-conceived in Paris, fell in love but feared they might be half-siblings due to limited sperm banks. French laws restrict genetic testing, forcing the couple to rely on an illegal doctor or a home kit ordered abroad. After confirming they were not related, Audrey discovered her biological sister was a client she had represented in court. Their DNA testing revealed four out of ten activists shared the same donor. Audrey eventually found her deceased donor, Philippe, through a genetic match. Their campaign contributed to legal changes allowing future donor-conceived individuals to access donor information. Despite these wins, France remains one of few European nations banning at-home DNA tests.
items.title: Donor-conceived couple in France tests for sibling relation

key_points: V. Kunhikrishnan rejected Pinarayi Vijayan's allegation that internal moves caused the CPI(M)'s defeat in Payyannur.
Kunhikrishnan stated the party leadership failed to correct organizational and political shortcomings he had highlighted for years.
He criticized district secretary K.K. Ragesh for defending the decision to field T.I. Madhusoodanan again and questioned fund utilization.
Kunhikrishnan affirmed his allegiance to communist ideology and truth rather than individual leaders, vowing his campaign would continue.
items.summary: Former CPI(M) leader V. Kunhikrishnan rejected Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan's allegations regarding internal party moves that allegedly caused the party's defeat in the Payyannur Assembly election. Speaking to The Hindu, Kunhikrishnan stated that the party leadership failed to address organizational shortcomings he had highlighted for years. He argued that voters heard arguments from both sides and chose him, rejecting claims that he was a tool of the enemy. Kunhikrishnan also criticized district secretary K.K. Ragesh for defending the decision to field T.I. Madhusoodanan again and questioned the utilization of party funds. He asserted that dissatisfaction with the CPI(M) extends beyond Payyannur, citing issues in the North Malabar Education Society and the Manu Thomas controversy. Kunhikrishnan affirmed his allegiance to communist ideology and truth rather than individual leaders, vowing that his campaign against perceived failures would continue regardless of threats or attempts to silence dissent.
items.title: V. Kunhikrishnan rejects Pinarayi's charge, says Payyannur verdict reflects Keralam CPI(M)'s failures

key_points: Minister Sharan Prakash Patil stated that more taluks will be added to the drought list after a comprehensive assessment.
The government will declare drought status strictly based on National Disaster Response Fund and State Disaster Response Fund criteria.
Gurmitkal and Yadgir taluks are being monitored and are likely to be added to the updated list.
Patil clarified that teacher suspensions adhere to civil service rules and criticized the BJP for exploiting the issue politically.
items.summary: Karnataka Minister Sharan Prakash Patil announced that additional taluks will be classified as drought-affected following a ground-truth assessment. The government will strictly apply National and State Disaster Response Fund criteria to determine eligibility. Currently, 101 taluks are listed, with Gurmitkal and Yadgir likely to be included in the second phase. Patil also addressed teacher suspensions, stating the action follows civil service rules and dismissing political accusations from the BJP.
items.title: Karnataka Minister adds drought-hit taluks after assessment

key_points: India and Uzbekistan have elevated their bilateral relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership, the ministry of external affairs said.
Both countries aim to take bilateral trade to $5 billion by 2030.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, to meet with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.
items.summary: India and Uzbekistan have elevated their bilateral relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership, the ministry of external affairs said. Both countries aim to take bilateral trade to $5 billion by 2030. Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, to meet with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.
items.title: India and Uzbekistan aim to boost bilateral trade to $5 billion by 2030

key_points: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav accused BJP and RSS leaders of acting on RSS instructions to oppose reservation.
Chirag Paswan demanded Jitan Ram Manjhi resign if he supported reviewing reservation policies.
Tejashwi Yadav challenged the ministers to contest elections from unreserved seats if they opposed reservation.
The dispute follows a Supreme Court judgment allowing states to create sub-categories within SC/ST reservations.
items.summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav criticized BJP and RSS leaders Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi for opposing reservation policies. Yadav alleged the two ministers were acting on RSS instructions while benefiting from reserved seats. He challenged them to resign and contest from unreserved seats if they truly opposed reservations. The remarks followed a public spat between Paswan and Manjhi regarding SC/ST sub-categorization. Paswan demanded Manjhi resign if he supported reviewing reservation, while Manjhi's son Santosh Kumar Suman offered to resign first. Yadav also referenced RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's 2015 call for a reservation review, noting Bihar voters rejected that idea. The controversy arises after a Supreme Court judgment allowing states to create sub-categories within reservations.
items.title: Tejashwi Yadav Criticizes BJP-RSS Over Reservation Dispute

key_points: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya has asked SEBI to probe the Sensex crash during the Closing Auction Session.
Somaiya attributes the volatility to a lack of liquidity after 3:15 pm and suggests suspending the CAS.
The former MP points out that separate auctions on NSE and BSE may fragment market liquidity.
He argues that the current auction band could cause significant valuation changes for large companies.
The article notes Somaiya's concern that cash and derivatives trading timelines differ during the auction.
items.summary: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya has requested the Securities and Exchange Board of India to investigate a sharp decline in the Sensex during the Closing Auction Session. The index fell over 2,000 points within minutes on August 27 before recovering. Somaiya attributes this volatility to insufficient liquidity after 3:15 pm and proposes temporarily suspending the CAS mechanism. He highlights concerns regarding separate auctions on NSE and BSE that may fragment liquidity. The former MP also questions whether the current auction band adequately protects large market capitalizations from significant valuation swings. Additionally, he notes discrepancies in trading timelines between cash and derivatives markets that could weaken arbitrage mechanisms. The Economic Times reports these observations and recommendations made by Somaiya in his communication.
items.title: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya seeks SEBI probe into Sensex volatility

key_points: Analysts expect fresh swings in bullion markets as investors track upcoming US jobs data and Eurozone inflation figures.
Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities noted that market volatility will persist while participants price in a potential September Federal Reserve policy change.
Recent data shows MCX gold futures fell 3.8% last week, while silver outperformed with a 21% gain in August.
Gaurav Garg of Lemonn Markets Desk highlighted silver's strong performance against gold.
Trivedi added that dollar movements and geopolitical headlines regarding the US-Iran conflict will determine whether gold stabilizes or faces further profit booking.

Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities noted that market volatility will persist while participants price in a potential September Federal Reserve policy change. Recent data shows MCX gold futures fell 3.8% last week, while silver outperformed with a 21% gain in August. Gaurav Garg of Lemonn Markets Desk highlighted silver's strong performance against gold. Trivedi added that dollar movements and geopolitical headlines regarding the US-Iran conflict will determine whether gold stabilizes or faces further profit booking.
items.title: Bullion braces for fresh swings as US jobs data, Iran tensions take centre stage: Analysts

key_points: Apple announced a $60 billion investment in Texas to bolster its US manufacturing network.
The new Houston plant will produce Mac mini computers and advanced artificial intelligence servers.
CEO Tim Cook described the initiative as the company's largest-ever American manufacturing commitment.
Apple expects gross margins to fall between 47% and 48% in the fiscal fourth quarter due to rising memory costs.
items.summary: Apple plans a $60 billion investment in Texas to strengthen its US supply chain as John Ternus prepares to become CEO. The company will build a Houston facility for Mac mini and AI servers but will not manufacture iPhones domestically. CEO Tim Cook stated this marks Apple's largest-ever American manufacturing program commitment. The strategy aims to protect profit margins against potential future tariffs while addressing rising memory costs.
items.title: Apple commits $60 billion to Texas supply chain under new CEO

key_points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told investors the company views AI expansion as a positive-sum evolution.
Wall Street fears triggered a market drop dubbed the 'SaaSpocalypse' that erased $1 trillion in value.
Salesforce reported strong recovery and deepened AI integration with Anthropic.
Palantir CEO Alex Karp warned enterprises to protect proprietary data when using AI providers.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated the company aims for a positive-sum evolution rather than destroying traditional software firms. This comment addressed Wall Street fears following a market drop dubbed the 'SaaSpocalypse' that erased $1 trillion in value. Salesforce reported strong recovery and deepened AI integration with Anthropic. Meanwhile, Palantir CEO Alex Karp warned enterprises to protect proprietary data when using AI providers.
items.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei reassures investors about enterprise software

key_points: About 3,500 displaced people are housed in temporary shelters across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.
The Kathmandu Post reported severe shortages of clean drinking water, sanitation, and essential medicines in the camps.
Medical officials warn that crowded shelter conditions could increase the risk of disease outbreaks.
Rescue teams continue searching for over 2,500 missing people as floodwaters recede in northern and central Nepal.
items.summary: Thousands of people displaced by Nepal's August 26 floods are living in temporary shelters without basic necessities. The Kathmandu Post reported that relief camps in Rasuwa and Nuwakot house about 3,500 people, though shortages of clean water and medicines persist. Doctors warn crowded conditions could increase disease risks. Families continue searching for missing relatives while infrastructure damage hampers relief operations.
items.title: Thousands displaced by Nepal floods face shortages in temporary shelters

Venkatesh, an international Bruce Lee Award recipient, demonstrated his skills in Kata and Sparring.
Organisers noted he is among the youngest masters in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to achieve this rank.
Venkatesh stated his goal is to make Nizamabad district number one in karate in Telangana.
items.summary: Karate master Edla Venkatesh of Nizamabad received his 5th Dan Black Belt at an examination conducted by Grand Master S. Srinivasan. Organisers noted he is among the youngest masters in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to achieve this rank. key_points: At least seven people died after a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus.
Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Unal Ustel confirmed 237 people were rescued.
The vessel began taking in water 15 minutes after departure due to bad weather.
A search is ongoing for another 24 people missing from the incident.
items.summary: A ferry capsized off northern Cyprus, killing seven people and rescuing 237 others. Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Unal Ustel stated the vessel began taking in water 15 minutes after leaving Kyrenia due to adverse weather. Turkish media reported at least seven deaths, while a search continues for 24 missing individuals. The Filo Denizcilik ferry sank near Diana beach after departing for the Turkish port of Tasucu.
items.title: Ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus, killing 7; 237 rescued

key_points: Dr Ashok Kumar Mittal stated there is no plan for a coalition with the Akali Dal.
The BJP intends to contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab on its own.
Mittal highlighted relief initiatives for Nepalese students affected by recent floods.
Sadhguru expressed grief over 80 deaths in Nepal and committed ₹1 crore to relief funds.
items.summary: Dr Ashok Kumar Mittal told India Today there are no plans for a BJP-Akali Dal coalition. The MP confirmed the party will contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats independently. Mittal also discussed relief efforts for Nepalese students and drug control measures. Meanwhile, Sadhguru mourned 80 flood victims in Nepal and pledged ₹1 crore aid.
items.title: Dr Mittal denies coalition plans with Akali Dal amid Punjab political news

key_points: Gujjar leaders reacted with outrage after the Armed Forces Tribunal deleted a two-year censure from Brigadier Padmasambhava Acharya's record.
The censure related to the custodial deaths of three civilians following an operation in Poonch district in December 2023.
Shahnawaz Choudhary described the tribunal's decision as a betrayal that mocks the judicial system and aids the officer's future promotion.
The tribunal dismissed the officer's argument that senior commanders in the control room should share responsibility for the excesses.
The Armed Forces Tribunal clarified that the deletion of the punishment record was an exception made under specific Ministry of Defence policy.
items.summary: Prominent Gujjar community leaders in Jammu and Kashmir expressed anger after the Armed Forces Tribunal removed punitive action against Brigadier Padmasambhava Acharya regarding the custodial deaths of three civilians in Poonch. The dispute stems from a December 2023 operation where security forces allegedly tortured detainees, leading to their deaths. While a Court of Inquiry censured the Brigadier for two years, the tribunal ordered the deletion of this record from his administrative file. Gujjar leader Shahnawaz Choudhary called the decision a "complete betrayal of the community," arguing it undermines accountability. Social activist Zahid Parwaz warned that shielding command responsibility sets a dangerous precedent. The tribunal dismissed the officer's claim that senior commanders shared blame, stating ground operations rest with the sector commander. Despite the deletion, the tribunal noted that excessive force against civilians remains prohibited under AFSPA guidelines.
items.title: Gujjar Leaders Outraged as Tribunal Clears Brigadier in Poonch Custodial Deaths Case

key_points: KDA Chairman Purushottama Bilimale expressed dismay over the lack of permanent memorials for Molahalli Shiva Rao and Shrinivas Mallya.
Bilimale stated the authority is ready to support initiatives to honor these leaders' contributions to the coastal region.
Data collected by the KDA shows 3,200 government schools were built in Karnataka between 1915 and 2024.
Bilimale noted that 1,970 schools have not included their names in property records of the land on which they were built.
items.summary: Kannada Development Authority Chairman Purushottama Bilimale expressed dismay over the absence of permanent memorials for Molahalli Shiva Rao and Shrinivas Mallya. Bilimale stated the authority supports initiatives to honor these leaders who built schools and infrastructure. He highlighted that 3,200 government schools were constructed in Karnataka between 1915 and 2024. Bilimale noted that 1,600 schools lack name inclusion in property records. The KDA Chairman praised a new book on Shiva Rao written by Aravind Chokkady.
items.title: KDA Chairman urges memorials for coastal leaders Molahalli Shiva Rao and Shrinivas Mallya

key_points: The HRCP reported that the PoK elections were marred by violence and allegations of rigging.
The commission criticized the state's disproportionate use of force and noted it could not independently verify casualty figures.
Communication restrictions and journalist arrests hindered independent verification of the electoral process.
India and the Indian MEA condemned the polls as a farce and a hollow exercise.
The HRCP called for an impartial investigation into deaths and the withdrawal of cases against peaceful activists.
items.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) reported that the recent elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir were compromised by violence and allegations of electoral manipulation. The commission's fact-finding mission attributed unrest to deep-seated political grievances and criticized the state's disproportionate use of force against protesters. While the government disputed casualty figures, the HRCP noted it could not independently verify the full scale of civilian deaths due to restricted access. The report highlighted severe communication blackouts and journalist restrictions that hindered independent verification of the electoral process. India and the Indian Ministry of External Affairs condemned the polls as a farce, citing the ongoing dispute over the region's status. The HRCP called for an impartial investigation into deaths and the withdrawal of cases against activists detained for peaceful assembly.
items.title: HRCP says Pakistan's PoK polls marred by violence and rigging claims

key_points: The Land Trust of Napa County bought the 2,300-acre former Walt Ranch for $24 million to create the Osos Ridge Preserve.
Funding came from the Land Trust, Craig and Kathryn Hall, the State Coastal Conservancy, the Wildlife Conservation Board, and the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation.
The preserve protects a vital wildlife corridor used by black bears, mountain lions, and other species across Napa County.
The site features oak woodlands, grasslands, and watersheds that support rare plants and Indigenous historical sites.
The Land Trust will partner with the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District to open the preserve to the public in spring 2027.
items.summary: The Land Trust of Napa County purchased the former Walt Ranch for $24 million to establish the Osos Ridge Preserve. The Land Trust of Napa County, Craig and Kathryn Hall, and various foundations funded the acquisition to prevent vineyard development. The property serves as a critical wildlife corridor for species like black bears and mountain lions. It contains diverse habitats supporting rare plants and key watersheds for the Napa River. The Land Trust will manage the site with the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District, opening it to the public in spring 2027.
items.title: Land Trust of Napa County buys 2,300-acre ranch for $24M to create public preserve

key_points: Railway police registered a murder case after finding a woman's body under a train seat in Dharwad, Karnataka.
Deputy Superintendent of Police Somashekar Juttal reported visible injuries on the victim's neck, face, and chest.
Police found no initial evidence of rape but are awaiting the autopsy report for further clarity.
Investigators are attempting to identify the woman and reconstruct her movements before she boarded the train.
items.summary: Railway police in Karnataka registered a murder case after discovering a woman's body concealed under a seat in a train's women's compartment. Deputy Superintendent of Police Somashekar Juttal stated the deceased, aged 30 to 35, had visible injuries on her neck, face, and chest. Authorities found no prima facie evidence of rape but are awaiting post-mortem results to determine the cause of death. Police are currently identifying the woman, who is believed to be from Maharashtra, and investigating her movements prior to boarding the train.
items.title: Police register murder case after woman's body found under train seat in Karnataka

key_points: Khalid Mohamed's new book details his thirty-year career as a film journalist who burned bridges with Bollywood stars.
The authors report that editor Fatma Zakaria created the pen-name Lens Eye to allow Mohamed to interview stars anonymously.
Mohamed expresses bitterness about the industry, noting that some stars still owe him fees for writing and directing films.
The reviewer states that the book offers straight, no-holds-barred insider stories of Mumbai's film world.
items.summary: A review of Khalid Mohamed's new book, Not Quite Family, explores his tumultuous thirty-year career as a film journalist and critic. The authors report that Mohamed describes how his close relationships with stars like Dilip Kumar and Amitabh Bachchan often turned to ignominy after he wrote unfavorable reviews. He explains that editor Fatma Zakaria created the pen-name Lens Eye so he could conduct interviews without facing the actors he critiqued. The book contains sympathetic pages about actress Smita Patil and details Mohamed's eventual ouster from the Times of India. Mohamed now distances himself from the industry, calling it petty and soul-deadening while noting that some stars still owe him fees. The reviewer notes that the book offers straight, no-holds-barred insider stories of Mumbai's film world.
items.title: Khalid Mohamed details his bitter thirty-year career as a Bollywood critic

key_points: The Ministry of External Affairs stated that 149 Indian nationals were rescued from Nepal as of August 30, 2026.
India deployed specialized tunnel technical contingents and forensic experts to assist in rescue and victim identification efforts.
Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah confirmed that 794 bodies had been recovered while 2,502 people remained missing.
Over 20,000 security personnel are conducting rescue operations, including 8,730 ground rescues and 3,081 air evacuations.
items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reported that 149 Indian nationals were rescued from flood-hit Nepal as of 5:30 pm on August 30, 2026. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed the number via a social media post. India has deployed specialized tunnel technical contingents and forensic teams to assist in search and rescue operations and identify victims. The fourth relief flight carried 11 tonnes of supplies, including blankets and hygiene kits. Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah stated that authorities are following directives for managing unidentified bodies, with 794 bodies recovered by Sunday evening. Rescue teams face significant challenges due to debris and rising water levels in areas like the Upper Trishuli complex. Nepal Police reported 2,502 people remain missing, including 933 hydropower workers and 592 foreign nationals. Over 20,000 security personnel are deployed, with ground forces conducting 8,730 rescues and air crews evacuating 3,081 people.
items.title: India rescues 149 nationals in Nepal floods as relief flights arrive

key_points: Lucknow authorities demolished twelve illegal lawyer chambers and continue operations on remaining sites.
Chandigarh Police are probing the abduction and murder of influencer Manjeet Kaur, who died from burn injuries.
Police suspect suspects Rinku, Shubhi, and Pinda in Kaur's death and are examining CCTV footage.
Lucknow Police detained a driver suspected of colluding with rivals in the killing of activist Dhirendra Pratap Singh.
items.summary: Lucknow Municipal Corporation demolished twelve illegal lawyer chambers and continues action on others following a High Court order. Chandigarh Police are investigating the murder of influencer Manjeet Kaur, who died after being abducted and set on fire. Authorities suspect three individuals in the case and are reviewing CCTV footage. Lucknow Police also detained a driver linked to the death of activist Dhirendra Pratap Singh.
items.title: Lucknow Demolishes Illegal Chambers; Chandigarh Police Probe Influencer Murder

key_points: Hindustan Times reports that Wall Street's current calm may fade as the VIX rises in September.
Yahoo Finance cites historical data showing the VIX often rises to around 18 by mid-September and about 19 in early October.
September is historically a weak month for the S&P 500, averaging a 0.6% decline since 1950.
Hindustan Times notes that October and November have historically produced gains, averaging 0.9% and 1.9% respectively across all years.
The article advises investors to watch how sharply volatility rises and what is driving it, as historical patterns do not guarantee 2026 will follow the same path as previous years.
items.summary: Hindustan Times reports that Wall Street's current calm may fade as the VIX rises in September. The CBOE Volatility Index fell to 14.13 on Friday, its lowest level of 2026, but historical data suggests volatility often increases from late August to early fall. Yahoo Finance cites that the VIX has historically risen to around 18 by mid-September and about 19 in early October. The article explains that a higher VIX indicates investors expect bigger market moves, which can be either higher or lower, rather than signaling a guaranteed crash. September is historically a weak month for the S&P 500, averaging a 0.6% decline since 1950, with an average 0.8% drop during midterm election years. However, October and November have historically produced gains, averaging 0.9% and 1.9% respectively across all years. Hindustan Times notes that while 2026 has seen a major volatility spike linked to Iran war headlines, the current low VIX reading gives the market room to become more volatile without necessarily indicating trouble. Investors are advised to watch how sharply volatility rises and what is driving it, as historical patterns do not guarantee 2026 will follow the same path as previous years.
items.title: Rising VIX signals potential end to Wall Street calm in September

key_points: At least seven people died when a ferry carrying about 267 capsized off Kyrenia.
Turkish Cypriot Prime Minister Unal Ustel confirmed the death toll via Anadolu news agency.
Rescue efforts saved 237 people while 23 remain missing.
Officials stated the cause of the capsizing remains unclear.
items.summary: Anadolu news agency reported at least seven deaths after a ferry capsized off Kyrenia. Turkish Cypriot Prime Minister Unal Ustel cited the incident involving 267 people aboard. Rescue teams saved 237 individuals while searching for 23 others. Officials stated the cause remains unclear as operations continue.
items.title: Seven Die After Ferry Capsizes Off Northern Cyprus

key_points: JNPA officials inspected key railway infrastructure along the Dedicated Freight Corridor route to assess operational potential.
The integration of Kharbhav and New Nilanje stations is expected to facilitate faster containerised cargo movement to Bhiwandi.
JNPA aims to increase the share of container traffic transported by rail to lower logistics costs and reduce turnaround times.
The initiative is part of broader efforts under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan to improve cargo-handling efficiency.
items.summary: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority is exploring strategic railway nodes to accelerate container evacuation from the port to the Bhiwandi logistics hub. Chairman Gaurav Dayal and Deputy Chairman Ravish Singh inspected facilities at Kharbhav, Bhiwandi Warehousing Hub, and New Nilanje stations. Officials stated that maximizing the Dedicated Freight Corridor aims to offer faster, sustainable routes while reducing logistics costs and road dependence. This initiative supports the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan for integrated infrastructure development.
items.title: JNPA Inspects DFC Rail Nodes to Speed Up Container Movement

The dog owner claimed the benches were already wet from rain and that her pets had used them for five years without issue.
The resident objected, stating the benches were used by people for yoga and that she had seen the owner fail to clean them previously.
Social media reactions were sharply divided, with some supporting the pet owner while others highlighted hygiene concerns regarding shared spaces.
items.summary: A disagreement between two women in a Thane housing society sparked an online debate after an argument broke out over pet dogs using a common bench. The dog owner claimed the benches were already wet from rain and that her pets had used them for five years without issue. The resident objected, stating the benches were used by people for yoga and that she had seen the owner fail to clean them previously. The incident escalated when the resident threatened to call security, prompting the owner to defend her pets as living beings. Social media reactions were sharply divided, with some supporting the pet owner while others highlighted hygiene concerns regarding shared spaces.
items.title: Woman Defends Pet Dogs Using Wet Bench in Thane Society

key_points: The death toll from flash floods in Nepal and China reached 768, with nearly 3,000 people still missing.
Nepal's disaster management authority reported 2,426 persons out of contact in the country, including 287 Indians.
India and China have sent rescue teams to assist with operations, including tunnel rescue and forensic identification.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority warned personnel to exercise caution due to rising floodwaters.
items.summary: AFP reported that the death toll from floods in Nepal and China rose to 768, with nearly 3,000 people missing. The country's disaster management authority stated 2,426 persons were out of contact in Nepal, while 546 were missing in Tibet. Rescue teams from India and China have arrived to assist with operations, including tunnel rescue and forensic analysis. Authorities warned personnel to exercise caution due to rising floodwaters in the Bhotekoshi river.
items.title: Nepal floods kill 768, leave nearly 3,000 missing as rescue continues

key_points: Police say three masked men burglarized the Delhi home of Congress leader Alka Lamba's 88-year-old father early Sunday.
The thieves reportedly fled with cash and jewellery after entering the property in daylight.
Lamba shared CCTV footage showing the suspects leaving the gate ajar on a single bike.
She questioned public safety in Delhi and stated the first lead has been handed to authorities.
