The thieves reportedly fled with cash and jewellery after entering the property in daylight. Lamba shared CCTV footage showing the suspects leaving the gate ajar on a single bike. She questioned public safety in Delhi and stated the first lead has been handed to authorities.
items.title: Three masked men burglarize Alka Lamba's father's Delhi home

key_points: A flash flood destroyed the Nepal-China border crossing on August 26, killing hundreds.
China's control over Tibet hinders real-time data sharing needed for disaster warnings.
Nepal's new government faces a test in maintaining strategic autonomy while rebuilding.
The author argues that border security priorities undermine effective disaster response.
Strengthening cross-border cooperation is essential to reduce future casualties in the region.
items.summary: A flash flood caused by a collapsed glacier destroyed the Nepal-China border crossing on August 26, killing hundreds and washing away villages and infrastructure. The article notes that China's strict control over Tibet creates significant obstacles for disaster response and information sharing. Nepal faces challenges rebuilding after the disaster, which tests the new government's ability to maintain strategic autonomy. China treats glacial data as strategically sensitive, preventing Nepal from receiving real-time warnings needed for safety. The author argues that border regions governed primarily for security suffer from inadequate disaster preparedness. Strengthening cross-border data sharing and early warning systems is essential to reduce future casualties. The piece concludes that states must prioritize people's safety over security anxieties to improve cooperation in the Himalayas.
items.title: China's Tibet controls hinder disaster cooperation after deadly Nepal flood

key_points: HNGIL issued a default notice to B9 Beverages for ₹11.77 crore in unpaid dues for customised glass bottles.
The brewer has 10 days to clear the debt or record a dispute before HNGIL initiates insolvency proceedings.
HNGIL alleges the unlifted stock has caused severe financial hardship due to its specific branding and specifications.
B9 Beverages remains out of production with an estimated total debt of ₹1,000 crore as restructuring continues.
items.summary: Hindusthan National Glass and Industries (HNGIL) has issued a default notice to B9 Beverages for alleged unpaid dues of ₹11.77 crore. The notice claims the brewer failed to lift over 51 lakh customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed orders. HNGIL stated that these branded bottles cannot be sold to other buyers, causing severe financial hardship. B9 Beverages now has 10 days to pay or record a dispute before HNGIL approaches the National Company Law Tribunal. Suraj Mehta, Chief Strategy Officer at HNGIL, said the company remains open to a resolution while the matter is under legal consideration. B9 Beverages has been out of production since September 2025 and carries an estimated debt of around ₹1,000 crore. Anicut Capital is leading the restructuring process alongside existing shareholders.
items.title: HNGIL issues default notice to B9 Beverages over unpaid glass dues

key_points: A massive flash flood on August 26 killed 734 people and left more than 3,000 missing in Nepal.
The disaster highlighted the absence of sustained, trans-boundary cryosphere data sharing between India and China.
Experts recommend a joint India-China-Nepal announcement of a Himalayan Glacial Hazard Early Warning System.
A pre-authorized Himalayan HADR compact is needed to enable rapid cross-border response without diplomatic delays.
items.summary: A catastrophic flash flood on August 26 killed 734 people and left over 3,000 missing in Nepal after a rock and ice collapse triggered a debris flow. The disaster destroyed critical infrastructure along the China-Nepal border and revealed a lack of sustained trans-boundary cryosphere data sharing between India and China. While Nepal mobilized its own rescue forces quickly, the event underscored the dangers of episodic glacial failures that cannot be tracked by rainfall alone. The article argues that India and China must establish a joint Himalayan Glacial Hazard Early Warning System and a pre-authorized humanitarian assistance compact to prevent future tragedies. Without open-source, glacier-specific data sharing, local residents and tourists remain vulnerable to these compound disasters.
items.title: Flash Flood in Nepal Highlights Need for India-China Data Sharing

key_points: US government debt has reached a record $40 trillion, increasing fears that high inflation will hurt stock returns and purchasing power.
Tom Essaye warns investors could face a 'lost decade' where portfolios lose real value due to persistent inflation rather than a market crash.
Essaye suggests investors consider shorter-term bonds, TIPS, and companies with strong pricing power to hedge against inflation risks.
The article notes that long-term bonds may struggle during high inflation as yields rise and existing bond prices fall.
items.summary: US government debt has reached a record $40 trillion, raising concerns that high inflation could erode investor purchasing power over the next decade. Tom Essaye, founder of Sevens Report Research, warns that instead of a market crash, investors may face a scenario where stock portfolios remain stable in nominal terms while inflation destroys their real value. Essaye notes that policymakers might allow inflation to reduce the real burden of debt rather than implementing painful spending cuts or tax increases. He points to the period between 1966 and 1981 as an example where high inflation caused real portfolio values to fall by around 50%. Essaye suggests investors consider shorter-term bonds, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, and companies with strong pricing power to protect against this risk.
items.title: US debt hits $40 trillion: Why high inflation could cause a ‘lost decade’ for stocks

key_points: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for 12 development projects in Lucknow Cantonment valued at approximately ₹101 crore.
The projects include a sports complex, a school for children with disabilities, additional classrooms, and robotic car parking.
Singh stated that these initiatives represent a commitment to public welfare rather than routine construction tasks.
The event marked the launch of the Chief Minister Abhyuday Yojana at Mangla Devi School and a city polyclinic at Ekta Bazaar.
items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for 12 development projects in Lucknow Cantonment valued at approximately ₹101 crore. The initiatives aim to modernise infrastructure and civic amenities, including a sports complex, a school for children with disabilities, and robotic car parking. Singh stated that these projects represent a commitment to public welfare rather than routine construction tasks. He highlighted the collaborative effort between the state administration, central authorities, and the industrial world to accelerate regional progress. The event also marked the launch of the Chief Minister Abhyuday Yojana at Mangla Devi School and a city polyclinic at Ekta Bazaar. Singh emphasised that true development involves ensuring access to education, clean water, and equal opportunities for all citizens.
items.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh lays foundation for 12 projects in Lucknow

key_points: Anand James identifies the Nifty as being in an accumulation phase unless it breaks below 24,000.
He forecasts a potential rally to 25,500 if the index breaks above 24,500.
James selects Ather Energy and Nazara Technologies as his primary stock picks for the week.
Options data shows strong support near 24,000 and resistance between 24,200 and 24,500.
items.summary: Anand James suggests the Nifty index is currently in an accumulation phase, provided it does not breach the 24,000 support level. He identifies a breakout above 24,500 as the trigger for a potential rally toward 25,500. James highlights Ather Energy and Nazara Technologies as his top buy ideas for the upcoming week. He notes that while Welspun Corp was a major August winner, Ather currently shows stronger momentum. The analyst also points to fresh put accumulation around 24,000–24,100, indicating trader caution. Conversely, call open interest clusters near 24,200–24,500 suggest resistance ahead. James maintains that holding above 1,560 keeps Ather's bullish setup valid, targeting 1,700. For Nazara, he expects a move to 405 as long as the stock stays above 364.
items.title: Anand James sees Nifty accumulation; picks Ather Energy and Nazara

key_points: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan has decided not to seek reappointment after 30 years with the lender.
The bank is fast-tracking the CEO appointment process to comply with regulatory requirements.
HDFC Bank's share price has fallen 27% this year, marking its worst performance since 2003.
The next CEO will need to address governance concerns and restore investor confidence.
Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha is reportedly among the top candidates to replace Jagdishan.
items.summary: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan announced his decision to step down, stating he will not seek reappointment when his term ends on 26 October. The bank is fast-tracking the search for a successor to address governance concerns and restore investor confidence. HDFC Bank's share price has fallen 27% this year, underperforming the broader banking index. The board is considering both internal and external candidates, with Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha reportedly among the top choices. The next CEO will face challenges including lingering issues from the MSRTC controversy and the fallout from Credit Suisse bonds. Analysts suggest a credible external candidate could help stabilize the stock price and navigate regulatory expectations.
items.title: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan steps down amid governance scrutiny

key_points: CJP national convenor Abhijeet Dipke indicated the leadership may consider reinstating Vijeta Dahiya.
Dipke described the incident leading to Dahiya's removal as insensitive despite calling him a nice person.
Dahiya was removed after videos surfaced showing him at a fast-food outlet during protests at Jantar Mantar.
The former spokesperson stated he felt made a scapegoat while defending the party against criticism.
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke stated that party leadership might bring former spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya back. Dipke acknowledged the timing of Dahiya's removal was wrong and insensitive. Dahiya was dropped after viral videos showed him at a fast-food outlet while protesters faced police violence. The former spokesperson claimed he was made a scapegoat while actively debunking propaganda against the party.
items.title: CJP founder says leadership may recall ex-spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya

key_points: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke at a Madison Square Garden event organized by AHEAD, attended by thousands of Indian-Americans.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the RSS for its exclusionary vision and divisive ideology.
Approximately 61 organizations stated the RSS does not represent their vision of Hinduism or India.
Activists protested outside the venue, accusing the RSS of promoting hate and violence against religious minorities.
items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed a crowd at Madison Square Garden for an event organized by AHEAD, drawing both enthusiastic support and significant opposition. While organizers highlighted themes of universal oneness and invited interfaith leaders, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the RSS for its exclusionary ideology. Approximately 61 organizations stated the RSS does not represent their vision of Hinduism, citing concerns over the group's history and alleged promotion of hate. Activists outside the venue protested the visit, linking the organization to violence against minorities and comparing its ideology to fascism. Despite these controversies, thousands of attendees gathered to hear Bhagwat speak on unity and dharma, illustrating a deep divide within the Indian-American community regarding the organization's role.
items.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Visits NYC Amidst Diaspora Division and Protests

Three mainboard IPOs will collectively raise over ₹1,265 crore.
Purple Style Labs IPO opens on August 31 with a price band of ₹546–₹575.

The list includes Purple Style Labs, Deepa Jewellers, Rays of Belief, and four SME issuers. Purple Style Labs will open on August 31 with a price band of ₹546–₹575 per share. Deepa Jewellers will open on September 1, 2026, with a price band of ₹168 to ₹177 per share. Eight other mainboard IPOs will debut, while three current offerings will conclude.
items.title: Seven new Indian IPOs open next week including Purple Style Labs

key_points: Apparel exporters claim rising cotton and yarn prices are damaging competitiveness and cancelling orders.
AEPC Chairman A. Sakthivel urges the Union government to regulate yarn exports.
Prices for cotton yarn have risen approximately 60% since January, widening the gap with Bangladesh.
Textile mills attribute the increase to a 26% jump in cotton prices.

Sakthivel urges the Union government to regulate yarn exports. Prices for cotton yarn have risen approximately 60% since January, widening the gap with Bangladesh. Textile mills attribute the increase to a 26% jump in cotton prices. Exporters note mills revise prices frequently without notice.
items.title: Apparel exporters warn yarn price hikes threaten export orders

key_points: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX is constructing a foundry in Bastrop, Texas, to manufacture turbine blades internally.
Musk claims this in-house casting capability could accelerate natural gas turbine deployment by up to 18 months.
The initiative addresses a critical bottleneck where only four companies worldwide can currently cast turbine blades at industrial scale.
Environmental groups report that gas turbines used by data centers emit hazardous pollutants affecting nearby communities.
Research suggests emissions from such facilities could cause millions of premature deaths annually in affected regions.
items.summary: Elon Musk announced that SpaceX is building a foundry in Bastrop, Texas, to cast turbine blades and vanes in-house. This move aims to accelerate natural gas turbine production by up to 18 months to address power grid constraints for AI data centers. Musk stated that natural gas remains necessary to supplement solar energy for several years while GPU shortages persist. However, this strategy faces significant environmental challenges, as gas turbines emit pollutants linked to respiratory diseases and cancer. In Memphis, the NAACP has accused SpaceX of operating turbines without required permits or pollution controls. Studies in Virginia indicate that emissions from similar facilities could harm millions of people and cause premature deaths annually.
items.title: Musk accelerates gas turbine production via in-house casting despite pollution concerns

key_points: Dr Simon Nieder argues that serious AI harms may arrive invisibly through ordinary decisions rather than sudden takeovers.
Dr Anthony Harris highlights that AI social dangers were identified decades ago and calls for interdisciplinary debate.
David Kyler states that fragmented national efforts will delay effective international AI controls and global treaties.
The letters collectively urge governments to establish minimum safeguards and human authority for consequential AI actions.
items.summary: Three letters to the editor argue that artificial intelligence risks require coordinated global action rather than fragmented national efforts. Dr Simon Nieder warns that severe harms may arrive quietly through incremental decisions rather than dramatic takeovers, suggesting governments agree on minimum safeguards for weapons and infrastructure. Dr Anthony Harris notes that AI dangers have been recognized since 1972 and calls for a debate involving both sciences and humanities. David Kyler, a former OpenAI employee, states that a global AI treaty is essential to prevent delays caused by disjointed approaches. He argues that opposition to datacentres diverts attention from establishing rigorous AI guardrails needed to pre-empt destructive outcomes.
items.title: Three writers argue for international AI governance and systemic safeguards

key_points: Caterpillar is applying its mining automation expertise to deploy AI in dynamic construction and quarry environments.
The company reported using the Cat AI Assistant to help technicians access repair procedures via voice commands.
Caterpillar plans to spend $100 million over the next five years to train its 118,000 employees in AI and robotics.
The firm reported second-quarter revenue of $20.5 billion, with power-generation sales spiking 72%.
items.summary: Caterpillar is leveraging decades of mining automation experience to deploy artificial intelligence across diverse industrial environments. The company reported using its Cat AI Assistant with field technicians and plans to invest $100 million over five years to train its 118,000 employees. Caterpillar CTO Jaime Mineart stated the firm aims to integrate AI into customer workflows while utilizing its 1.6 million connected assets. The industrial giant noted its second-quarter revenue reached an all-time high of $20.5 billion driven by data center equipment demand.
items.title: Caterpillar applies mining automation experience to broader AI deployment

key_points: A randomized experiment at Bocconi University involving 1,053 freshmen found that GPT-4o significantly improved student grades on a business assignment.
A separate lesson on causal reasoning encouraged more diverse and unusual solutions without raising traditional scores.
Researchers noted that current grading rubrics favor polished, conventional answers over originality and deep reasoning.
The authors explicitly state that whether AI use actually improves learning remains an open question due to the lack of follow-up tests.
items.summary: A randomized experiment at Bocconi University involving 1,053 freshmen found that GPT-4o significantly improved student grades on a business assignment. The study revealed that while AI enhanced output quality, a separate lesson on causal reasoning encouraged more diverse and unusual solutions without raising traditional scores. Researchers noted that current grading rubrics favor polished, conventional answers over originality and deep reasoning. The authors explicitly state that whether AI use actually improves learning remains an open question due to the lack of follow-up tests. Additional research cited indicates that when AI replaces student thinking, long-term exam performance often declines. The study concludes that grading systems must evolve to reward originality and reasoning rather than just structural completeness.
items.title: Bocconi study finds AI boosts grades but learning remains unproven

The event includes thousands of deals on tech, fashion, and home goods.
Apple products like the iPhone 17 Pro and AirPods Pro 3 are featured with price reductions.
Amazon plans to release new featured deals daily through the end of the sale.
items.summary: Amazon has officially launched its 2026 Labor Day Sale, featuring thousands of discounts across various product categories. The event will run for ten days, concluding on September 7. The retailer highlights significant price drops on Apple products, including the AirPods Pro 3 and iPhone 17 Pro models. Additionally, the sale offers deals on tech gadgets, home goods, and game day essentials. Prices range from under $5 for pantry items to over $1,000 for premium electronics. Amazon will update featured deals daily throughout the weekend and into next week.
items.title: Amazon launches 2026 Labor Day sale with thousands of tech deals

key_points: An online article links Elon Musk's budget cuts to the cancellation of Nepal's disaster monitoring resources.
Former USAID head Jeremy Konyndyk stated that canceled projects removed flood prediction and early warning capabilities.
The Nepal flood has resulted in 752 confirmed deaths and 2,502 missing people according to current reports.
The US Department of State provided $3.6 million in humanitarian assistance to flood-affected households in Nepal.
items.summary: An online commentary connects Elon Musk's role in the Trump administration to the Nepal flood disaster. The author argues that Musk's budget-cutting office canceled disaster risk reduction projects in Nepal. Former USAID head Jeremy Konyndyk stated that these cuts eliminated flood prediction and early warning systems. Konyndyk noted that while the Nepal flood might be an outlier, similar climate hazards are occurring in the US. The article highlights that the Nepal flood has caused 752 confirmed deaths and 2,502 missing people. Meanwhile, the US Department of State provided $3.6 million in humanitarian assistance to Nepal. The author contrasts this aid with billions spent on other initiatives.
items.title: Online Army Links Elon Musk Budget Cuts To Nepal Flood Disaster

key_points: Nearly 2,700 Electrek readers responded to a survey about the competitive threat of the Ford Fathom to Slate Auto.
Most respondents felt it was too soon to determine the outcome since neither vehicle is currently on the market.
Several commenters identified Ford's dealer network as a potential weakness compared to Slate's direct sales strategy.
One user argued that Ford's past delays in EV charging standards have already damaged consumer confidence in the brand.
items.summary: Electrek surveyed nearly 2,700 readers about whether Ford's upcoming $30,000 Fathom electric pickup would destroy Slate Auto before launch. The majority of respondents remained non-committal, citing that neither truck is available yet or that price differences matter to some buyers. However, several commenters argued that Ford's traditional dealer network acts as a significant handicap compared to Slate's direct sales model. Others noted the spiritual similarity between Slate's approach and the original Model T, predicting Slate could succeed where Ford struggles with pricing. One user suggested the real threat to Slate is not the truck itself, but the chilling effect of Ford's announcement on potential orders. The article concludes by highlighting how Ford's history of delaying EVs for charging standards may have damaged consumer trust.
items.title: Electrek readers debate if Ford Fathom will kill Slate Auto

key_points: Planned gas-fired power capacity tied to data centers nearly doubled in the first half of 2026 alone.
Amazon, Nvidia, and Microsoft are building or planning massive gas plants to power their data centers.
A June report from Business Insider found that data centers permitted through 2025 could use between 224.3 and 358.8 terawatt-hours of electricity annually.
A recent report from Semafor warns that supply bottlenecks and political pressure could lead to a cool-off period for data center development.
items.summary: Data center expansion for artificial intelligence is causing a rapid revival of natural gas power capacity in the United States. Major tech companies like Amazon, Nvidia, and Microsoft are securing new gas-fired plants to meet their energy demands. However, experts warn that supply bottlenecks and public opposition could slow this growth. The surge in energy consumption is shifting costs to residential customers while raising concerns about emissions and decarbonization goals.
items.title: Data Centers Drive Massive U.S. Natural Gas Power Buildout

key_points: Turkey and Saudi Arabia signed an agreement to add 3 GW of renewable energy capacity, bringing Turkey's total planned capacity to 5 GW.
Saudi Arabia will invest $2 billion in two solar farms in Sivas and Karaman to meet the electricity needs of 2.1 million households.
Turkey aims for renewables to generate 47 percent of its electricity by the end of the decade, with solar expected to become the largest source by year-end.
The government plans to offer at least 2 GW of wind and solar capacity through annual auctions to accelerate its 2035 target of 120 GW combined capacity.
items.summary: Turkey and Saudi Arabia announced a new agreement to add 3 GW of renewable energy capacity to Turkey, raising the nation's total planned capacity to 5 GW. Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar stated that Saudi Arabia will invest $2 billion in two solar farms in Sivas and Karaman, which will serve 2.1 million households. The deal involves external financing from international institutions and marks a significant step in Turkey's energy diversification strategy. While hydropower remains the largest renewable source, the government aims for renewables to supply 47 percent of electricity by the end of the decade. Turkey currently relies heavily on coal, which accounts for 34 percent of generation, though solar output has doubled since 2023. Officials expect solar to become the country's largest electricity source by year-end as auctions for additional wind and solar projects proceed.
items.title: Saudi Arabia and Turkey Sign Deal to Add 3 GW of Renewable Energy

The Santa Fe EREV is expected to exceed 600 miles of combined range with dual electric motors.
Hyundai plans for conventional hybrids to represent 50% of its total sales by 2030.
The author notes that many consumers still prefer traditional hybrids over fully electric vehicles.
items.summary: Hyundai announced plans to introduce extended-range electric vehicles to the United States, beginning with the Santa Fe. The company claims the new powertrain offers over 600 miles of combined range and acceleration comparable to fully electric vehicles. Hyundai's luxury division, Genesis, will also adopt this technology, with the GV70 expected to achieve 640 miles of range. The Santa Fe will be manufactured in Alabama, while the GV70 will be produced in South Korea. Hyundai stated it aims to sell half its total volume as conventional hybrids by 2030. The article notes that other manufacturers like Stellantis, Ford, and Volkswagen are also developing similar powertrains. The author concludes by observing that consumer range anxiety persists despite the environmental benefits of electric vehicles.
items.title: Hyundai Plans Extended-Range Electric Vehicles for US Market

key_points: An analyst identifies Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing as the likely ultimate winner in the AI hardware race.
The author notes that major chip designers like Nvidia and AMD must farm out manufacturing to TSMC.
Research by The Motley Fool indicates TSMC accounted for approximately 72% of global foundry revenue at the end of 2025.
TSMC CEO C.C. Wei stated that elevated chip demand is expected to continue through at least 2029 or 2030.
items.summary: An analyst argues that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing will be the ultimate winner in the AI hardware race. The author states that Nvidia and AMD design chips but rely on TSMC for manufacturing. According to The Motley Fool research, TSMC held about 72% of global foundry revenue at the end of 2025. CEO C.C. Wei expects elevated chip demand to last through at least 2029 or 2030. The article concludes that TSMC is a safe investment regardless of which AI model dominates.
items.title: Analyst argues TSMC will win the AI hardware race as a foundry

key_points: Michael Burry bought Nvidia call options while expanding his short stock position, calling the move a hedge.
Benzinga reported that Burry stated the trade relies on his existing large short and put positions to offset risk.
CNBC reported that Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $2.22 per share, beating the $2.09 consensus estimate.
Nvidia guided to 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, nearly double what analysts had expected.
items.summary: Michael Burry purchased Nvidia call options while simultaneously increasing his short position in the stock, describing the trade as a hedge rather than a bullish bet. Benzinga reported that Burry stated he would not have executed the move without his existing large short and put positions to offset risk. The strategy coincided with Nvidia's recent earnings beat, where the company reported adjusted earnings of $2.22 per share and guided revenue growth of 70% for fiscal 2028. CNBC reported that Nvidia's revenue climbed 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, significantly exceeding Wall Street expectations.
items.title: Michael Burry buys Nvidia calls while maintaining short stock position

key_points: Google updated US maps to show Lake America following a presidential order.
The name change applies only to users within the United States.
Canadian and international users will still see the lake labeled as Lake Ontario.
The update coincides with ongoing trade disputes and 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods.
items.summary: Google updated its US maps to display Lake Ontario as Lake America, adhering to a directive from President Donald Trump. The tech giant stated the change follows the US Geographic Names Information System and applies only to users within the United States. While the name appears as Lake America in the US, it remains Lake Ontario for Canadian and international users. This move mirrors a previous policy adjustment regarding the Gulf of Mexico. The renaming occurs amidst escalating trade tensions, including recent 50 percent tariffs imposed by Trump on Canadian products. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney defended the original name, noting its Indigenous origins and historical significance. Conversely, Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed the order as a joke, asserting the lake will always be known as Lake Ontario.
items.title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America following US presidential order

key_points: Twenty-nine US states have filed a lawsuit accusing Meta of designing addictive features for children.
The case specifically targets features such as infinite scrolling, notifications, and recommendation algorithms.
Meta faces potential fines totaling $1.4 trillion if the lawsuit is successful.
The outcome could fundamentally change how social media platforms design their core engagement tools.
items.summary: Twenty-nine US states have accused Meta of intentionally designing Facebook and Instagram to keep children hooked. The lawsuit alleges the company engineered features like infinite scrolling and notifications to exploit young users. Meta faces potential fines totaling $1.4 trillion if it loses the case. The outcome could fundamentally alter how social media platforms design recommendation algorithms and user engagement tools.
items.title: Twenty-nine US states accuse Meta of designing addictive features for children

key_points: Bloomberg ranks Tim Cook 46th among CEOs while Elon Musk leads the list.
Tim Cook earned $74.3 million in total compensation from Apple in 2025.
Tim Cook's net worth of $838 million is far below Elon Musk's $20.5 billion.
items.summary: Bloomberg data shows Tim Cook ranked 46th among CEOs with $74.3 million in 2025 compensation. His net worth of $838 million trails Elon Musk's $20.5 billion significantly.
items.title: Bloomberg ranks Tim Cook 46th among CEOs while Elon Musk leads

key_points: President Trump threatened to report NBC journalist Kristen Welker to the FCC for characterizing his endorsement results as mixed.
Trump posted a chart on Truth Social claiming 98 percent of his endorsed candidates won, which he attributed to Welker's inaccuracy.
Welker hosted the 2020 presidential debate and currently anchors NBC's Meet the Press program.
The Trump administration has recently used court subpoenas to compel journalists to reveal confidential sources regarding national security stories.
items.summary: President Donald Trump announced he will report NBC journalist Kristen Welker to the Federal Communications Commission for allegedly misrepresenting his endorsement results. In a Truth Social post, Trump criticized Welker's description of his primary endorsements as having mixed results and shared a chart claiming 98 percent of his endorsed candidates won. He stated that her comments regarding public airwaves were inaccurate and warranted regulatory action. Welker, who hosts Meet the Press, previously engaged in a heated exchange with Trump during a June interview where he labeled major networks as crooked. This threat follows a broader pattern of Trump targeting media outlets through FCC reviews and defamation lawsuits. Additionally, the administration has recently used court subpoenas to pressure journalists into revealing confidential sources for national security stories.
items.title: Trump threatens to report NBC journalist Kristen Welker to FCC

key_points: Jon from Cardiff launched a uniform swap scheme to help parents manage rising school uniform costs.
The initiative now involves over 200 schools and has facilitated 8,000 clothing exchanges.
Jon estimates the platform could save Welsh families more than £50m per year.
The scheme aims to normalize second-hand clothing and reduce the stigma of asking for help.
Government regulations in England will limit secondary school uniforms to three logo items starting in September.
items.summary: Jon from Cardiff established a free school uniform swap shop to assist families facing the cost-of-living crisis. The initiative has grown from a single school to over 200 schools, facilitating the exchange of 8,000 items since its website launched in March. Jon estimates the platform could save Welsh families more than £50m annually, addressing an average uniform cost of £343 for primary and £442 for comprehensive pupils. Participants report that the scheme effectively removes the stigma associated with second-hand clothing while promoting sustainability. The project also connects parents within their communities and complements existing government measures to limit uniform costs in England.
items.title: Cardiff father expands school uniform swap shop to 200 schools

key_points: The Guardian editorial states that China blocked rare earth exports to Japan in 2010, prompting global concern.

items.title: American man says he is moving to India over healthcare costs

This move mirrors a previous update for the Gulf of Mexico. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the renaming, noting the Indigenous origin of the name Ontario.

India and Uzbekistan agreed to elevate their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership.
The leaders set a target of $5 billion in annual trade by 2030.

They agreed to an annual trade target of $5 billion by 2030, up from the current volume of over $1 billion. items.title: PM Modi receives 36th international honour as India-Uzbekistan trade targets $5B

key_points: Indian Army Aviation pilots evacuated a casualty from a steep slope at 18,600 feet near the Nun Kun massif.
The Fire & Fury Corps stripped the aircraft of non-essential equipment to minimize weight for the flight.
Pilots executed a perilous hover, touching down with only one skid on the snow-covered slope.
The Fire & Fury Corps is the only military formation that regularly deploys mechanized forces at such extreme altitudes.
items.summary: Indian Army Aviation pilots performed a daring casualty evacuation at 18,600 feet in Ladakh's Zanskar range. The Fire & Fury Corps stated that the team stripped the helicopter of non-essential gear to fly in severe winds with no landing space. Pilots maintained a perilous hover, touching down on one skid on a steep, snow-covered slope. This mission highlights the corps' unique capability to operate mechanized forces in extreme high-altitude environments.
items.title: Indian Army pilots execute high-altitude helicopter rescue in Ladakh

key_points: The Worli Police Camp Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal marked the start of its 77th Ganeshotsav festival.

items.title: India Women defeat Thailand Women by 94 runs in T20 Asia Cup

No midnight loudspeaker permission is granted for the remaining days of the Ganpati festival.

The permitted dates are September 15, 18, 19, and 25, covering the period from 6 am to 12 midnight. This exception applies only to these four days, while other festival days remain subject to standard noise pollution rules. items.title: Mumbai mandals granted midnight loudspeaker permission on four 2026 Ganpati visarjan days

The transition from BBMP to the Greater Bengaluru Authority has slowed approval processes significantly.
Capital gets locked up before construction begins, eroding returns before a shovel goes into the ground.
Office demand remains strong with vacancy rates declining across top cities including Bengaluru.
Experts suggest better coordination and digital scrutiny could improve approval predictability.
items.summary: Bengaluru's commercial real estate market is experiencing significant delays between securing statutory clearances and starting construction. Developers attribute these bottlenecks to the administrative transition from BBMP to the Greater Bengaluru Authority, which has slowed approval processes. Mid-stream rule changes and idle contractors have increased costs and uncertainty for projects. While office demand remains strong with vacancy rates declining, the approval stage continues to lock up capital before construction begins. Experts suggest that better coordination between authorities and digital scrutiny could improve predictability and execution timelines.
items.title: Bengaluru commercial projects face approval delays squeezing new supply

key_points: Microfinance loans often fail to create new businesses and instead increase competition among existing small enterprises.
High interest rates and the use of loans for immediate survival needs prevent many borrowers from achieving financial independence.
Relying on multiple loans frequently leads to debt juggling rather than productive investment in rural areas.
The modernization of microfinance has paradoxically made land collateral a requirement, endangering the assets of the poorest farmers.
Experts argue that sustainable economic development requires skills and infrastructure support alongside access to capital.
items.summary: The article argues that microfinance has failed to deliver promised economic independence for many low-income households in Asia. Experts state that flawed assumptions about capital access and entrepreneurial potential often lead to ineffective policy interventions. Evidence from India suggests loans frequently boost existing businesses instead of creating new ones, while high interest rates in places like Bangladesh strain borrowers. Research indicates that multiple loans often result in debt juggling rather than productive investment, leaving families financially vulnerable. Additionally, the sector's shift toward using land as collateral risks putting farmers' primary assets at risk. The authors conclude that broader support for skills and infrastructure is essential, noting that debt is inappropriate for households lacking sustainable returns.
items.title: Microfinance loans often increase debt rather than creating economic freedom for the poor

key_points: NSE average daily turnover fell 3 per cent to ₹1,16,579 crore in August, marking a five-month low.
The new Closing Auction Session mechanism triggered sharp price swings in the Nifty and BSE Sensex on expiry days.
Former SEBI Chairman UK Sinha stated that better preparation and beta testing were needed before implementing the framework.
Analysts attributed reduced trading volumes to uncertainty over final closing prices and widespread profit-booking.
items.summary: NSE cash market volumes fell to a five-month low in August amid uncertainty over the new Closing Auction Session mechanism. Average daily turnover dropped 3 per cent to ₹1,16,579 crore as sharp index swings and profit-booking dampened investor appetite. SEBI introduced the CAS framework on August 3 to determine official closing prices for 208 stocks. Former SEBI Chairman UK Sinha suggested better preparation was needed but expects the system to stabilize. Analysts noted that while the BSE saw a recovery, the NSE remains more affected by the disruption.
items.title: NSE cash volumes hit five-month low as CAS swings unsettle investors

The two nations set a target of USD 5 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed Tashkent for Bishkek to attend the 26th SCO Summit following a two-day state visit to Uzbekistan. He thanked President Mirziyoyev for strengthening India-Uzbekistan ties and elevated the relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The leaders agreed to increase bilateral trade to USD 5 billion by 2030 and cooperate on critical minerals and digital infrastructure. Modi also paid tribute to former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri and received Uzbekistan's highest honour, the Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order.
items.title: PM Modi leaves Uzbekistan for SCO Summit after bilateral talks

key_points: Subhash Chandra stated that borrowers repaid ₹3,803 crore of the ₹4,808 crore funds they received.

items.summary: Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra addressed social media concerns regarding his personal insolvency by detailing repayment figures and guarantee amounts. He stated that borrowers repaid ₹3,803 crore of the ₹4,808 crore they received, leaving a balance of ₹998 crore. Chandra explained that while total personal guarantees signed amounted to ₹22,000 crore, the current claims filed by lenders stood at ₹5,311 crore. He noted that some lenders had already received full repayment but still submitted claims to the National Company Law Tribunal. The chairman clarified that the repayment plan was prepared by a court-appointed Resolution Professional and highlighted that his family sold assets to assist with repayments. Chandra expressed hope that lenders would reconcile outstanding accounts with borrowers to recover the remaining dues.
items.title: Subhash Chandra clarifies personal guarantee repayments in NCLT insolvency case

key_points: The review identifies 'The Hunt' and 'Ma, Let's Fly' as the strongest stories in the collection.
Other stories are criticized for relying on clichés or failing to deliver dramatic impact.
The reviewer concludes the book is a highly uneven collection with missed opportunities.
The collection explores themes of desire, memory, and the consequences of both.
items.summary: A review of Pratyaksha's new collection, The Mistress of Phoolpur, notes that while some stories offer interesting ideas, the overall execution falls short. The author reports that two stories, 'The Hunt' and 'Ma, Let's Fly', successfully explore themes of desire and family dynamics. However, the reviewer argues that other tales rely on clichés or fail to deliver dramatic impact. The book maps fault lines between restraint and transgression but remains highly uneven. Ultimately, the collection provides a few sparks of inspiration alongside several forgettable tales.
items.title: Review finds uneven quality in Pratyaksha's short story collection

key_points: Northern Railway evacuated at least 391 passengers and 40 crew members following a hill slip on the Kalka-Shimla route.
Incessant rain undermined the track between Koti and Ghumman stations, exposing part of a bridge.
Four incoming trains were short-terminated, and over 400 people were transported via buses and a rescheduled train.
The railway reported that the rescue operation resulted in zero inconvenience and no passenger complaints.
items.summary: Northern Railway rescued more than 400 passengers and crew after incessant rain caused a hill slip between Koti and Ghumman stations. The incident exposed part of a bridge and short-terminated four incoming trains. Officials evacuated travelers using buses and a specially rescheduled train. The railway stated the operation was seamless with no complaints or refund requests.
items.title: Northern Railway rescues over 400 passengers after hill slip halts Kalka-Shimla train

Police officials stated the boy was handed to his mother for safety and advised the family to be more careful. The boy vowed to continue the protest until the Prime Minister meets him.
items.title: Six-year-old Bihar boy stages dharna over 'police excesses' against parents

key_points: Chevron is using proprietary chemical surfactants in more than 600 wells to enhance oil recovery.
Ovintiv reports a 9% productivity improvement in Permian wells treated with surfactants.
Diamondback Energy invested $30 million to test surfactant treatments on 60 wells.
Chevron plans to license its technology to ZL Chemicals for broader commercialization.
Industry leaders view these chemical cocktails as critical for maintaining shale production growth.
items.summary: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers are using advanced chemical surfactants to increase oil recovery from existing wells. Chevron has deployed these treatments in over 600 wells, starting with the Permian Basin. The company plans to license its technology to ZL Chemicals for broader market application. Ovintiv reports a 9% productivity improvement in treated wells, while Diamondback Energy tests the method on 60 wells. Industry executives describe these chemical mixtures as essential for unlocking remaining oil trapped in rock formations.
items.title: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers use soap cocktails to boost oil output

key_points: Lucid recalled 27,185 vehicles for a potential fire risk related to exterior LED lighting.
A July software update already fixed the overheating issue by limiting current to the circuits.
Over 20,700 affected vehicles had received the update as of August 20.
The recall involves three identified fire events and multiple smoke-related incidents linked to front lighting.
items.summary: Lucid Motors issued a recall for 27,185 Air vehicles due to a potential fire risk involving exterior LED lighting. The issue stemmed from software that failed to properly limit current to the lights, which could cause overheating. Lucid notes that a July software update already addressed this problem by reducing amperage and preventing repeated re-energizing of faulty circuits. As of August 20, over 20,700 affected vehicles had received the update, while the remainder will receive notices in October. The company has identified three fire events and several smoke-related incidents linked to the front lighting system. While owners were advised to park outside pending repairs, the fix is simply an available software update rather than a physical part replacement. The article highlights that most vehicles were already updated before the recall was officially filed.
items.title: Lucid recalls 27,185 vehicles for LED fire risk fixed by July software update

key_points: UBS strategist Sagar Khandelwal urged clients to position for a commodity upcycle.
The firm cites electrification, AI infrastructure, and supply constraints as key drivers.
UBS recommends diversified exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals, and agriculture.
The Quantix Commodity Index Total Return gained more than 22.5% since late June.
items.summary: UBS strategist Sagar Khandelwal advised clients to position for a commodity upcycle driven by electrification, AI spending, and supply constraints. The firm believes hard assets offer structural returns and portfolio protection against inflation and energy disruptions. Khandelwal recommends maintaining diversified exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals, and agriculture. Recent data shows the Quantix Commodity Index Total Return surged over 22.5% since late June.
items.title: UBS strategist urges clients to position for a major commodity upcycle

key_points: XPENG reported Q2 revenue of $2.91 billion with a gross margin of 20.7%, though it posted a net loss of $200 million due to increased R&D costs.
The company launched VLA 2.0 version 6.3.0, claiming a 300% latency improvement and 20x safety performance gains through new inference and prediction capabilities.
XPENG's robotics division, Dogotix, secured $900 million in funding to deploy IRON humanoid robots in retail and service sectors by 2027.
The automaker is leveraging local AI processing on dedicated Turing chips to enable full voice control and address regulatory challenges in intelligent driving.
items.summary: XPENG has announced significant advancements in its physical AI technology alongside strong second-quarter financial results. The company reported revenue of $2.91 billion, an 8.0% year-over-year increase, while its gross margin reached 20.7%. Despite a net loss of $200 million driven by higher R&D spending, XPENG is positioning itself as a technology firm through partnerships with Volkswagen Group and a new robotics division. The automaker recently launched VLA 2.0 version 6.3.0, which features a 300% improvement in latency and 20x better safety performance. This update enables proactive reasoning up to 21 seconds into the future and allows for full voice control of vehicle functions. Additionally, XPENG's robotics unit, Dogotix, raised $900 million in funding to support the commercialization of its IRON humanoid robot. The company plans to deploy these robots in retail and service sectors starting in 2027. XPENG aims to create an AI flywheel where better cars generate more data, leading to improved software and further sales. By running advanced AI models locally on dedicated chips, the company seeks to overcome regulatory and privacy challenges while expanding its technology services revenue.
items.title: XPENG Unveils VLA 2.0 AI, Secures $900M Robot Funding, and Reports Q2 Growth

Pricing is expected to start at $230,150, with deliveries to US buyers scheduled for 2028. items.title: Bentley Unveils Its First In-House All-Electric Torcal SUV

Management intends to use these investments to secure supply chains and support long-term growth. items.title: Tesla faces cash flow risk from heavy spending on robotaxis and robots

items.summary: The New York Times reports that Western export bans have not reduced demand for brand-name SUVs and trucks in Russia. items.title: Russia imports stolen Canadian trucks via criminal networks

items.summary: Alexis Abramson argues that UK solar bonds could lower capital costs for rooftop solar installations. key_points: Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodriguez defended a controversial energy agreement with Donald Trump, asserting the nation retains full ownership of its oil reserves.
Trump announced the historic transaction, claiming it will fill the US Strategic National Reserves and double American oil holdings.

items.summary: Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodriguez defended a controversial energy agreement with Donald Trump, asserting the nation retains full ownership of its oil reserves. Rodriguez stated the deal aims to generate over $209bn in revenue and transform Venezuela into an energy powerhouse. Trump announced the historic transaction, claiming it will fill the US Strategic National Reserves and double American oil holdings. The agreement reportedly involves Washington taking control of 65bn barrels from 17 strategic oilfields. The deal has sparked outrage among Venezuelan opposition figures and former officials who condemn it as a neocolonial land grab. Critics argue the pact undermines democratic prospects and compares the state oil company to a US subsidiary. Rodriguez countered accusations of surrendering resources, emphasizing the need for investment to convert underground wealth into national development.
items.title: Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez defends controversial oil deal with Donald Trump

key_points: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman telescope from Florida to study dark energy and exoplanets.

items.summary: NASA successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman telescope from Florida on Sunday to investigate dark energy, black holes, and exoplanets. The agency states the telescope offers a field of vision 100 times larger than Hubble and James Webb. Nicky Fox, a NASA administrator, noted the mission aims to discover up to 100,000 new exoplanets to answer if humanity is alone in the universe. The spacecraft separated from its SpaceX rocket and is traveling to an orbit one million miles from Earth. Astronomer Jenifer Millard explained the distant orbit prevents infrared interference from Earth and the Moon. Named after NASA's first female executive, the telescope has a five-year primary lifespan with a goal to operate for 10 years.
items.title: NASA launches Nancy Grace Roman telescope to explore dark energy and exoplanets

items.summary: Niger's ruling military junta restored order in Niamey after mutineers stormed the presidential palace and a military air base. State TV reported that dozens of soldiers were killed or arrested following the unrest. Loyalist forces, aided by Russia's Africa Corps, repelled the attackers who had taken hostages and fired at sensitive sites. The mutiny, which lasted from Friday into Saturday, was driven by grievances over rising insecurity and jihadi violence in the Sahel region. Analysts noted that deteriorating security conditions have fueled discontent within the armed forces. Russia's Africa Corps intervened with ground and aerial support to neutralize the mutineers. Regional allies, including the Alliance of Sahel States, Algeria, and Turkey, expressed solidarity with Niger's leadership.
items.title: Niger junta suppresses mutiny with Russian Africa Corps support

key_points: A BBC investigation exposed a WhatsApp group with 532 members used to arrange hundreds of millions of euros in cash transfers.
Belgian authorities linked the network to Islamic State financing, people smuggling, and drug trafficking.
Six money launderers were convicted in a 2024 Belgian court case after investigators found the group on a suspect's phone.
Austrian police dismantled a separate hawala network connected to people smuggling that transported about 100,000 people into Europe.
items.summary: A BBC investigation with the European Broadcasting Union revealed a massive hawala network operating through a WhatsApp group called 'Traders of Greater Europe.' The group, containing 532 members, facilitated over 82,000 messages and millions in cash transfers between February and December 2022. Belgian magistrate Vincent Guerra described the scale as staggering, noting the network extended globally. The system was used for organized crime, people smuggling, and funding Islamic State militants, including payments to help IS wives escape detention. Six money launderers, including network head Abu Adam, were convicted in a 2024 Belgian court case. Investigators found evidence of at least 12,000 transactions and thousands of photos of cash and IDs. Similar networks in Austria were linked to human trafficking operations transporting approximately 100,000 people into Europe.
items.title: BBC exposes WhatsApp hawala network moving millions for crime
